statement.p: Convert from rectangular to polar coordinates:
Note: Choose r and \theta such that r is nonnegative and 0 \leq \theta \lt 2\pi

static.solution:
\mathbf{(a)} The point (3,0) is on the positive x axis distanced 3 units from the origin. Hence, r=3 and \theta=0.
Thus, (r,\theta)=(3,0)
\mathbf{(b)} The point (3,\frac{3}{\sqrt{3}}) is in the first quadrant so \theta = \tan^{-1} \left(\frac{\frac{3}{\sqrt{3}}}{3}\right) = \frac{\pi}{6}.
Also, r=\sqrt{{3}^2+\left({\frac{3}{\sqrt{3}}}\right)^2} = \sqrt{12} Hence, (r,\theta)=\left(\sqrt{12},\frac{\pi}{6}\right)
\mathbf{(c)} The point (-2,2) is in the second quadrant. Hence, { \theta ={ \tan}^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{-2}\right) = {\tan}^{-1}(-1)=\pi -\frac{\pi }{4}=\frac{3\pi }{4}}. Also, r=\sqrt{{(-2)}^{2}+{2}^{2}}=\sqrt{8}. Hence, \left(r,\theta\right)=\left(\sqrt{8},\frac{3\pi }{4}\right).
\mathbf{(d)} The point \left(-1,\sqrt{3}\right) is in the second quadrant, hence, \theta ={\tan}^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{-1}\right)= \tan^{-1}\left(-\sqrt{3}\right)=\pi -\frac{\pi }{3}=\frac{2\pi }{3}. Also, r=\sqrt{\left(-1\right)^{2}+{\left(\sqrt{3}\right)}^{2}}=\sqrt{4}=2. Hence, \left(r,\theta \right)=\left(2,\frac{2\pi }{3}\right).
